newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air to upgrade international service.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air to upgrade international service.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc is expected to announce Tuesday schedule changes that will capitalize on its existing international partnerships, analysts said.
Delta said it will host joint news conferences in New York and London on Tuesday to announce "major enhancements" to its international service.
"These service enhancements will strengthen Delta's position as the number one U.S. carrier across the Atlantic," Delta said in a prepared statement.

"Airlines typically make schedule adjustments every quarter. They will probably adjust the transatlantic routes to align better with their code-sharing arrangements," said Helane Becker, an airline analyst with Smith Barney.
Delta has existing code-sharing arrangements with Air France and Virgin Group's Virgin AtlanticAirways.
Delta also recently expanded its agreements with Sabena, Swissair, and Austrian Airlines.
Under the expanded joint operation agreement, the four airlines will have open reservation systems, revenue sharing and standarized fares and booking categories.

Delta and other U.S. carriers have been scrambling to make their international operations stronger to combat competition from the pending alliance between British Airways Plc and AMR Corp's American Airlines.
Delta's press conference will be held Tuesday at 0900 EST/1400 GMT at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York. The London news conference will occur at the same time at the Royal Aeronautical Society.
